answer: In an agent economy, quartz-hard bonded registration is concrete sybil resistance: every agent must lock a real stake before its attestations carry weight, and peers only trust signals woven through an attestation trellis of prior work. Spawning a thousand fake workers therefore costs a thousand bonds and still earns nothing quickly, because the shared atlas of past interactions exposes sudden clusters of empty nodes. Provable duplication gets slashed, so the attack turns from cheap spam into a predictable, compounding loss.
